translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

The August Ming established the civil service examinations in imitation of the ancient teaching of the Six Arts, consulting also the inherited institutions of successive dynasties, with the desire to recruit both civil and military talents and employ them. Having decreed that the realm should hold the triennial presentation of worthies, of the five hundred men recommended from the prefectures and counties in all, one out of five was to be selected and conferred an office. Still considering this insufficient, the Emperor further commanded the competent authorities that for three consecutive years, from the renzi year (1372) to the jiayin year (1374), three hundred men should be presented as tribute each year, and only when reaching the yimao year (1375) should the original system be restored; such imperial grace is most abundant indeed. Earlier, the Capital Region had complied in holding the Provincial Examination, and those who passed numbered seventy-two. Before they could be presented to the Southern Palace [Ministry of Rites for the Metropolitan Examination], His Majesty, in his earnest desire for good governance, selected and employed them all, to the point that some became Investigating Censors. translation_en: …Kai 凱 and the others received the command and withdrew, mutually admonishing one another in the hope of fulfilling His Majesty's intent. We thereupon agreed to divide the examination papers by Classic to assess them, and then cross-checked and decided upon them together so that there would be no cause for regret, before submitting them to the Chief Examiners. After the Chief Examiners had read through them all and ranked them in order, still fearing the lament of leaving pearls behind in the vast sea, they re-examined the papers that had already been rejected and exercised the utmost care over them. By day we exhausted our strength, and as night approached midnight, with candle shadows flickering between the screens and tables, we did not dare take our ease. Of the one hundred and eighty-nine scholars who sat for the examination, more than a hundred were selected. 萬邦咸寧夫賢之在野無以

府故昔人謂進士為將相科

punctuated: 編簡以傳。《書》有之：「野無遺賢，萬邦咸寧。」夫賢之在野，無以自見，多由進士而升名于天府，故昔人謂進士為將相科。姑以宋言之，深沉有德如王旦，面折廷争如寇準，出當方面如張詠，盖不可以勝數，至今科目倚之以為重。與茲選掄者，當思以前脩自勗，以忠貞佐國家，而致黎民於變時雍之治，庶於明體適用之學，或無所愧。不然，則是錄之行，他日將有指其名而議之者矣，可不
translation_en: … into a volume to be handed down. It is said in the Book of Documents (Shu): "When no men of worth are left neglected in the countryside, all the myriad states enjoy peace." Indeed, when men of worth are in the countryside and have no means of making themselves known, it is mostly through the status of metropolitan graduate (jinshi) that their names are raised to the imperial repository. For this reason, people of former times called the metropolitan graduate degree the "examination for generals and chief councilors." To speak provisionally of the Song dynasty: men of deep composure and virtue such as Wang Dan 王旦, men who rebuked the ruler to his face and contended in court such as Kou Zhun 寇準, and men who went out to take charge of regional commands such as Zhang Yong 張詠 were truly too numerous to count; down to the present day, the examination system relies on them for its prestige. Those who participate in this selection ought to reflect on exhorting themselves after the example of those former worthies, assisting the State with loyalty and integrity, and bringing about a governance in which the black-haired people are transformed and live in harmony; thus, perhaps, they will have nothing to be ashamed of with respect to learning that illuminates fundamental principles and meets practical needs. Otherwise, when this record is circulated, in days to come there will be those who point to their names and criticize them. How can they not…

Agriculture and sericulture are the means by which the people are nourished; how can the systems of land limitation (xiantian), equal-field (juntian), personal-share land (koufen), and hereditary-property land (shiye) be properly determined? The establishment of offices is the means by which administration is overseen; between relying on laws and relying on men, which is the more far-sighted counsel for governing the state? The selection of scholars is the means by which officials are appointed; between recommendation and election (xuanju) and seniority qualifications (zige), which is the essential method for the Ministry of Personnel (quancao)? Salt and iron are great sources of profit for the state; how can illicit practices be eradicated and abuses removed? Grain transport by water (caoyun) is a grand policy of the state; how can it suffice for the state while enriching the people?

The state seeks only practical results and does not value empty rhetoric. Please examine these matters in the light of antiquity and verify them against the present day, so that your words may certainly be put into practice, and when practiced, may serve as a model for the empire and future generations. Answer with your whole heart, and hold nothing back.
